headline: High-risk filesystem and git overlap in Claude Code with broad egress; Opik’s limited profile leaves interaction uncertainty, so cascading and compliance risks are bounded but nontrivial.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code ingests repo files and user-provided directories by default and can use MCP servers; Opik exposes a REST API and broad network egress. If Opik outputs are copied into files or MCP-fed content, Claude Code may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The shared bridge is plausible, but not documented directly.
conditions: IF Opik output is written into a repo file or MCP-fed source that Claude Code reads, injection becomes reachable.
IF Claude Code parses that content as instructions rather than data, prompt hijack is possible.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Opik outputs into Claude Code-readable files.
Require provenance tags or delimiters on any Opik-derived text.
Review MCP server inputs before enabling them.
Use a separate workspace for Opik artifacts.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code reads and writes local files, shell environment, and git history, while Opik has broad network egress and REST API access. If shared workspace data includes secrets or sensitive code, Opik can transmit it off-host. The pair creates a realistic leakage path through the shared filesystem, though no direct evidence shows automatic exfiltration.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared cwd or repo, Claude Code can access them.
IF Opik sends those artifacts to its REST API or another remote service, data leaves the host.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace before running either agent.
Use a scrubbed clone with only necessary files.
Block Opik from receiving raw file contents unless required.
Rotate any credentials found in git history.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Opik is not runnable here but still has broad network egress and a REST API surface. The pair shares mutable workspace state via filesystem and git, so concurrent edits can clobber each other. Because Claude Code runs as the invoking user with no self-isolation, the conflict can corrupt work irreversibly.
conditions: IF both agents touch the same repo or cwd concurrently, file and git conflicts are reachable.
IF Opik writes back derived artifacts into the shared workspace, overwrite races can occur.
mitigations: Serialize access to the repo with a lock file.
Assign separate working directories per agent.
Pause one agent while the other commits git changes.
Review and merge diffs manually before commit.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code and modify git state, while Opik’s evaluation/observability role suggests it may consume outputs for analysis or reporting. If Opik treats Claude Code’s output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream reports or actions. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Opik ingests Claude Code-generated text as ground truth, unverified errors can propagate.
IF downstream automation acts on Opik reports, the cascade can affect commits or operational decisions.
mitigations: Require human review of Opik outputs before action.
Add a verification step that checks Claude Code claims against source files.
Mark generated content as untrusted in Opik pipelines.
Limit Opik to read-only evaluation mode.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code explicitly handles git credentials and local files, while Opik’s profile does not show regulated-data handling or residency constraints. No direct compliance mismatch is documented, so only a low-risk gap exists if sensitive code or credentials are processed through a less controlled REST path. The other agent is not cited beyond its lack of such fields.
conditions: IF regulated data or credentials are placed in the shared workspace, compliance review is required.
IF Opik retains or transmits those artifacts outside approved boundaries, policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Confirm retention settings for Opik before use.
Avoid placing credentials in files Opik can access.
Document the data classes each agent may touch.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls to the pipeline.
